headline: Recursive video retrieval reports higher frozen-VLA success on perturbed simulation tasks
summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint reports Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), which indexes one task demonstration into four read-only levels—keyframes, phases, moments and short clips—and lets a planner retrieve detail for its current subgoal. The authors report HarnessVLA success rising from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus. These are author-reported simulation results: on LIBERO-PRO the RV-ICL arm used 50 episodes while prior-work baselines used 100, and the paper’s reported significance statistic does not yet have a recovered matched-data audit. On LIBERO-Plus the methods were compared on a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants. The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens on that comparison; physical-robot transfer is untested.
